To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified three genes in rice that encode proteins with homologies to the yeast p34cdc2 protein kinase, that these three genes are expressed in young seedlings, and that one of these genes,cdc2Os1, complements a yeast mutant ofCDC28.
two rice cDNAs encodingcdc2 homologue proteins have been isolated, and that one of these is a functional homologue of the yeast and mammalianscdc2 kinases.

the cDNA library was prepared using cultured rice cells, and the two genes, cdc2Os1 and cdc 2Os2, were isolated using PCR amplification, that the genes are expressed in young rice seedling, and that cdc2Os 1 could complement a yeast mutant of cdc2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization and functional analysis of rice homologues of yeast and mammaliancdc2+/CDC2 kinases.
the isolation and characterization of cDNAs encoding the cell cycle protein kinases of rice.
the isolation and characterization of cDNAs encoding the p34cdc2 kinase from rice (Oryza sativacv. japonica).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rice genome has at least three genes that encode structurally related but functionally distinct homologues ofcdc2.
there are three distinct rice genes that encode structurally related but functionally distinct cell cycle kinases.
the present study has demonstrated the existence of at least three distinct genes encoding the cell cycle regulatory kinase, cdc2, inOryza sativain addition to the previously reportedR2 gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rice genome contains at least three distinct genes for the p34cdc2 kinase, and that the rice genome also contains at least one gene for the p40CDC25 protein kinase, which is required for the activation of p34cdc2.
the cdc2Os and R2 genes in rice encode functionally distinct, but structurally related, protein kinases that play a role in cell cycle regulation.
there are at least two functionally distinct cdc2 homologues in rice, and that they are differentially expressed during the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two genes are expressed in a similar manner in the cell cycle, and that they are both required for cell cycle progression in the plant.
the cell cycle in rice is regulated by multiple homologous and non-homologous cell cycle kinases.

the rice cdc2 gene family is more complex than the yeast or animal cdc2 gene families, and that the rice cDNA clones that we have identified represent a subset of the genes that encode cdc2 homologues.
